b: Rising out of the rural landscapes of Tuy Phuoc, Xuan Phong Church presents an intriguing architectural cross-pollination that defies conventional ecclesiastical design.

Originally established as a modest thatched sanctuary in the late nineteenth century, the current structure was erected around 1890 using repurposed ancient Cham bricks salvaged from the nearby Binh Lam area, creating a tangible physical bridge between Catholic history and the region's medieval Champa heritage.

Most striking is its facade, dominated by three towering spires whose tapered geometric profiles distinctly mirror the iconic silhouette of traditional Cham towers, while church archives have also drawn structural comparisons to Khmer temple architecture.

Recently restored in a vibrant white-and-purple palette, this enigmatic house of worship stands as a captivating anomaly: a active Christian church built from the literal stones and stylized form of a long-vanished empire.
